proposed_statement_changes.reason: The current headline hard-wires the Choi--Yuan block event and an obsolete log-power-seven Gaussian approximation.  The corrected claim conditions first on the exact remainder event, uses the singular-covariance-safe 2022 fourth-root log-power-five theorem, and retains the Choi--Yuan expression only as an explicit specialization.  This narrows the headline interpretation to a finite-error transfer and preserves asymptotic coverage only under the displayed remainder and feasible-score probabilities.

The present question incorrectly compares the note's event-transfer class with the full published model and asks an upper-band conclusion without the unresolved uniform feasible-score premise.  The corrected question keeps the upper experiment on the baseline event-transfer slices, requires converse witnesses to lie in the explicit common subclass of array-plus-selected-functional objects, and requires those witnesses to prove score stability.  The common class is a subclass of the published approximate-rank class after law projection; upper validity does not transfer in the reverse direction without an approximation-bias remainder.

proposed.name: \(\mathfrak M^{\mathrm{CY},0}\) (baseline event-transfer class)
proposed.construction: \(\mathfrak M^{\mathrm{CY},0}=\{(P_n)_{n\ge1}:\mathsf A_{\mathrm{ind}}((P_n))\wedge\mathsf A_{\mathrm{ctr}}((P_n))\wedge\mathsf A_{\mathrm{subG}}((P_n))\wedge\mathsf A_{\mathrm{var}}((P_n))\wedge\mathsf A_{\mathrm{rowvar}}((P_n))\wedge\mathsf A_{\mathrm{vrep}}((P_n);\varepsilon^{\mathrm{vrep}})\wedge\mathsf A_{\mathrm{rank}}((P_n))\wedge\mathsf A_{\mathrm{inc}}((P_n))\wedge\mathsf A_{\mathrm{sig}}((P_n);\varepsilon^{\mathrm{sig}})\wedge\mathsf A_{\mathrm{spec}}((P_n);\varepsilon^{\mathrm{spec}})\wedge\mathsf A_{\mathrm{block}}((P_n);\varepsilon^{\mathrm{block}})\wedge\mathsf A_A((P_n))\wedge\mathsf A_B((P_n))\wedge\mathsf A_{\mathrm{nd}}((P_n))\wedge\mathsf A_{\mathrm{lev}}((P_n);\varepsilon^{\mathrm{lev}})\}\). Every member property holds at each finite \(n\) with the common event-transfer constants and fixed envelopes in the symbol table.  This exact-rank, blockwise-uniform, row-heteroskedastic class is not the published Choi--Yuan approximate-rank class; the superscript records the provenance of the block coefficients.

proposed.name: \(\mathfrak M^{\mathrm{CY}}\) (band event-transfer class)
proposed.construction: \(\mathfrak M^{\mathrm{CY}}=\{(P_n)_{n\ge1}\in\mathfrak M^{\mathrm{CY},0}:\mathsf A_{\mathrm{rem}}((P_n);\varepsilon^{\mathrm{rem}})\}\). Equivalently, each finite slice obeys \(\Delta_{\mathrm{CY},n}(K)\sqrt{\log(2K)}\le\varepsilon_n^{\mathrm{rem}}\) for the fixed vanishing envelope.  This condition controls only the deterministic primitive expression; asymptotic band validity still requires the separately displayed remainder-event and feasible-score failure probabilities to vanish.

open_obligations.what_is_open: Compute the exact signed second-order remainder of the specified Choi--Yuan estimator on a balanced rank-one complete array in \(\mathfrak M^\cap\), determine whether it is \(o(\Delta_{\mathrm{CY},n}(K))\), and prove both an attained \(1-\eta_n\) quantile lower bound and feasible-score stability for the same counterarray.
open_obligations.obstruction: Proposition A.4 supplies an upper perturbation envelope after several norm inequalities, not an attained expansion.  The frozen estimator construction names the nuclear-norm and debiasing procedure but does not specify its tuning rule, KKT solution, or signed second-order map.  First-order coefficients and the two-horizon covariance witness therefore do not determine the nonlinear remainder or its sign.  The frozen assumptions also contain no rowwise loading rate for the leave-one-cell-out feasible score.
open_obligations.attempted: The class-scope obstruction was removed: the published model was encoded as an array plus one selected functional, the actual event-block correspondence was stated, and a balanced rank-one array was shown by direct rate substitution to lie in a nonempty common subclass.  On that array the primitive ratios, leverage, marginal scale, and published six hypotheses were computed.  These calculations still leave the estimator's second-order KKT remainder unidentified, so neither a reverse perturbation inequality nor undercoverage can be inferred from the first-order witness.

prose_updates.tldr: The note's exact-rank, row-heteroskedastic model is now explicitly an event-transfer class, not the published Choi--Yuan class.  The eligible blocks aggregate exactly into one event-by-cell score, and a generic remainder event \(\mathcal R_n(u)\) yields a finite whole-curve error contribution \(P_n\{\mathcal R_n(u)^c\}+Cu\sqrt{\log(2p)}\).  Chernozhukov--Chetverikov--Kato--Koike's 2022 singular-covariance-safe theorem sharpens the Gaussian component to log power five and gives the balanced-loading elbow \(\log(Km)=o(m^{1/5})\).  Feasible growing-curve coverage remains conditional on the displayed remainder-event and score-stability probabilities.  The published approximate-rank, i.i.d. homoskedastic selected-functional class and the event-transfer class are incomparable; their explicit balanced rank-one common subclass is nonempty, but the attained nonlinear-remainder frontier remains open.

project_justification.gap: Published low-rank MNAR inference treats one block, entry, or selected scalar functional.  Choi--Yuan's staggered Theorem 3.2 attaches six conditions to one chosen group, time, and subgroup partition; it does not provide a growing event-path remainder probability or the rowwise feasible-score rate needed here.  Generic high-dimensional approximation does not supply those panel-specific controls.
project_justification.niche: The useful bridge is a primitive-cell event score with exact staircase covariance and a generic finite-error transfer that exposes the nonlinear remainder event and score discrepancy.  Class comparison must be made after pairing the published law array with its one selected functional.
project_justification.fill: The note fixes eligible-unit weights, proves exact block aggregation and shared-cell covariance, concentrates oracle unit variances, and bounds covariance, scale, and correlation errors deterministically by the feasible-score discrepancy.  The 2022 CCKK theorem gives Gaussian error \(C\{L_n(K)^2\log^5((p\vee3)m)\}^{1/4}\); anti-concentration adds \(Cu\sqrt{\log(2p)}\) on \(\mathcal R_n(u)\).  The Choi--Yuan bound enters only through \(\mathcal A_n(C)\subseteq\mathcal R_n(C\Delta_{\mathrm{CY},n}(K))\) and its unsimplified source-submodel union bound.  An explicit proposition proves class incomparability and nonemptiness of a balanced rank-one common subclass.

sampling_model.units: The inferential model is a complete triangular array in the note's exact-rank event-transfer class, with common regularity constants, fixed vanishing finite-slice envelopes, and independent centered sub-Gaussian errors on \(\mathcal Q_n^+\).  Variances are time-invariant within unit but may differ across units.  This is distinct from the published Choi--Yuan comparator, whose objects pair a law array with one selected scalar functional and use an approximately low-rank mean plus i.i.d. homoskedastic noise.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: The feasible implementation uses blockwise Choi--Yuan completion and debiasing, leave-one-cell-out untreated residuals, unit-level residual variances, plug-in influence coefficients, and Gaussian multipliers.  Oracle variance concentration is proved, while imputation contamination and the normalized rowwise loading discrepancy remain explicit through \(d_i\) and \(r_n^{\mathrm{score}}\).  The generic band theorem conditions on \(\mathcal R_n(u)\) and \(\mathcal B_n(h)\); neither event is made high probability by definition.

prose_updates.related_work: Choi and Yuan, \cite{ChoiYuan2024MNAR}, allow \(M^{\mathrm{pub}}=M^\star+M^R\) with a globally incoherent low-rank signal and i.i.d. homoskedastic sub-Gaussian noise.  Their published staggered Theorem 3.2 has six hypotheses for one selected \(\mathcal G,t_0,\{\mathcal G_\ell\}\), while Proposition A.4 supplies the one-block expansion used here.  Aggregation over growing eligible blocks yields only the displayed finite union bound.  Chernozhukov, Chetverikov, Kato, and Koike (2022), Theorem 2.1, doi:10.1214/22-AOS2193, supplies the singular-covariance-safe fourth-root approximation with log power five.  The separate 2023 nearly-optimal theorem is not used because its covariance nondegeneracy condition is unavailable for staircase scores.  Chernozhukov, Chetverikov, and Kato, \cite{ChernozhukovChetverikovKato2013Maxima}, Lemma 3.1, supplies singular-safe Gaussian covariance comparison, and \cite{ChernozhukovChetverikovKato2014Bands} supplies anti-concentration.  Choi, Kwon, and Liao, \cite{ChoiKwonLiao2024Completion}, cover fixed scalar functionals under additional conditions, not the frozen growing rowwise score discrepancy.  Ben-Michael and Feller, \cite{BenMichaelFeller2026Discussion}, motivate the right-to-carry event curve; Callaway and Sant'Anna, \cite{CallawaySantAnna2021DID}, obtain simultaneous staggered paths under parallel trends rather than low-rank MNAR completion.  Yan and Wainwright, \cite{YanWainwright2024Entrywise}, and Xia, Yan, and Wainwright, \cite{XiaYanWainwright2024ACA}, provide entrywise or scalar inference rather than this conditional growing-path transfer.
prose_updates.interpretation: For a right-to-carry event curve, the common critical value is justified only after the analyst controls the exact nonlinear remainder event and the realized score discrepancy.  Shared donor and pre-treatment cells remain in the full covariance.  Under balanced loadings, the Gaussian part allows \(\log(Km)=o(m^{1/5})\), but this does not certify either missing panel-specific probability.  A converse on the explicit common subclass would apply to the published model, whereas the event-transfer upper theorem does not cover published approximation bias from \(M^R\).
prose_updates.technical_internal_limitation: The primitive Choi--Yuan expression controls a one-block upper perturbation bound, not an attained nonlinear remainder and not a simultaneous heterogeneous-block event.  Its direct union bound may fail to vanish.  Variance replication controls the oracle residual squares but not the leave-one-cell-out imputation errors or the normalized rowwise loading discrepancy.  Therefore neither \(\|\rho_n\|_\infty=O_{P_n}(\Delta_{\mathrm{CY},n}(K))\) nor \(r_n^{\mathrm{score}}=o_{P_n}(\log^{-2}(2K))\) is asserted over the event-transfer class.  The common rank-one array verifies both class condition families, but the estimator's exact signed second-order KKT expansion is absent from the frozen primitives; the early-kill comparison and attainable frontier remain open.  Approximate-rank upper validity would additionally need an explicit \(M^R\) bias remainder.
prose_updates.honest_scope: The causal target is the eligible-cohort unit-share event curve under deterministic staggered adoption.  Settled results are the exact eventwise influence identity, full staircase covariance, oracle variance concentration, deterministic feasible-score stability, and a generic finite-error Gaussian-multiplier transfer with the 2022 log-power-five approximation.  The Choi--Yuan specialization supplies only the deterministic inclusion \(\mathcal A_n(C)\subseteq\mathcal R_n(C\Delta_{\mathrm{CY},n}(K))\) and an unsimplified i.i.d. homoskedastic source union bound.  Coverage tending to \(1-\alpha\) is conditional on explicit remainder and score probability limits.  The inferential event-transfer class is incomparable with the published approximate-rank selected-functional class.  Serial dependence, tuning selection, uniform feasible-score stability, simultaneous block probability, approximation-bias transfer, and the attainable nonlinear-remainder frontier remain open.
